name: _test_optional_intlist
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::_test_optional_intlist(Tensor values, int[]? addends) -> Tensor. This definition models only that one overload; the original Gems pytest defines the full contract (all overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation) and must not be narrowed to this signature. Other registered signatures, verbatim: aten::_test_optional_intlist.out(Tensor values, int[]? addends, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics evidenced by the tests: the operator is CPU-only and has two natively valid call forms. With addends=None it is a zero-copy identity that returns the operand object itself (res_out is values), preserving shape, stride, storage offset and dtype, never writing to the operand, and returning a writable alias; it also accepts strided/transposed/non-zero-offset and empty operands, and all special values (nan/inf) pass through untouched. With addends given it performs a 1-D int32 elementwise add with int32 wraparound, requiring a 1-D int32 operand of rank 1 and at least one addends entry per element (extra entries ignored, a tuple accepted); it returns a fresh int32 tensor (not an alias of the operand) that follows the operand's shape, and leaves the operand unmodified. addends is an optional value (None allowed) but is a required argument: omitting it raises. Rejected inputs raise RuntimeError/TypeError for non-int32 values, non-1-D values, non-tensor values and tensor addends; a short addends list raises RuntimeError/IndexError. There is no autograd formula, so backward raises 'derivative for aten::_test_optional_intlist is not implemented'. The .out overload (keyword-only out) writes in place, resizes a caller buffer of differing length in place, returns the caller's buffer (res is out), preserves strided/non-zero-offset geometry, and rejects non-int32 out buffers.
